hero.title: Everyone deserves a second chance.
hero.lead: At Hogares Victoria we walk alongside people facing addiction, offering shelter, support and hope so they can begin again.

manifesto.label: Our motto
manifesto.body1: The people who do the accompanying at Hogares Victoria know this road from the inside. We do not talk about addiction as somebody else's problem: we talk about something we have been through, with its impossible days and its steps backwards.
manifesto.body2: That is why our way of helping does not begin with a diagnosis. It begins with a conversation. Listening without judging, sharing a meal, going along to an appointment, picking up the phone. Everything else comes afterwards, at each person's own pace.

intro.label: About us
intro.title: A home can be where a new story starts.
intro.body1: Hogares Victoria is a non-profit civil association, Christian in inspiration, devoted to the shelter, guidance and whole-person support of people affected by addiction and social vulnerability.
intro.body2: We work with people facing difficulties related to drugs, alcohol, gambling and other addictions, and with their families too. According to the documentation published by the association, this work is provided free of charge.
intro.body3: Christian faith is part of who we are and of how we understand the dignity of every person. Nobody needs to share it to be welcomed here.

programs.label: What we do
programs.title: Close by, at every stage.
programs.lead: A home to live in, someone to talk to, a family to hold steady, and a constant presence in the places nobody else reaches.

impact.label: 2025 results
impact.title: What our annual reports say.
impact.lead: These figures come from the 2025 Annual Activity Report, signed by the directors of the association. They cover that year alone.
impact.note: We do not add these categories together: the same person may have taken part in more than one programme over the course of the year.

stories.label: Stories
stories.title: Voices that have already walked this road.
stories.lead: Testimonies, interviews and video published by the organisation itself. Nothing here is re-enacted or scripted.

history.label: Since 1986
history.title: It began in Barrios Altos, Lima.
history.body1: On 30 April 1986, Hogares Victoria — then known as Centro Victoria — opened its doors in Barrios Altos, in central Lima, to support young people affected by alcohol and drugs.
history.body2: Almost forty years later, that work continues in several countries and, since 2023, in Madrid as well. Luis and Vangie Salazar founded Hogares Victoria Internacional; the Spanish project is led by Pastor Alfredo Pedraza Soriano.

donate.label: Get involved
donate.title: Your support can be part of a new story.
donate.body: With your help we can keep offering shelter, food, support and opportunities to people who need to begin again.
donate.transparency: In 2025 the association received no public funding at all. Everything that sustains this work comes from members, donors and the sale of crafts made in our own workshops.

closing.title: Hope is something we build together.
closing.body: Whether you are looking for help or want to offer it, the conversation starts here.

acogida.name: Residential care
acogida.short: Somewhere to live while everything else is rebuilt.
acogida.intro: The heart of our work is the residential programme at the home in Quijorna, where people going through withdrawal and rehabilitation live together with daily support.
what: Work on healthy habits and personal responsibility.
acogida.who: Adults facing addiction who are willing to take part in a model built on shared living, shared responsibility and close day-to-day support.
acogida.note: Places are limited and availability changes. The best first step is simply to talk to us.

acompanamiento.name: Personal support
acompanamiento.short: Someone to talk to, inside the home and beyond it.
acompanamiento.intro: Alongside the residential programme, the association offers guidance and follow-up throughout the process. The 2025 report records this as individual and group sessions, and as an outpatient programme.
what: Group sessions built on mutual support.
Spiritual accompaniment, for those who want it.
Ongoing follow-up of each person's process.
acompanamiento.who: People going through rehabilitation, whether or not they live in the home, and those who have recently left it.
acompanamiento.note: This support is social, educational and spiritual. It does not replace medical treatment or professional psychological care. When a situation calls for it, we refer people to specialist services.

familias.name: Support for families
familias.short: Addiction never affects just one person.
familias.intro: Families are part of the process, and they carry its weight too. That is why the association runs dedicated family support sessions: 82 of them during 2025.
what: Support and guidance sessions for relatives.
Space to understand what is happening and what can realistically be expected.
Family involvement in the process, where it is possible and helpful.
familias.who: Mothers, fathers, partners, children, siblings and anyone close to a person living with addiction.

calle.name: Street outreach and prevention
calle.short: Going to where people are, before anyone asks for help.
calle.intro: Part of our work happens outside the home: in parks, stations and encampments where drug use is active. The aim there is not to convince anyone of anything, but to show up, listen, and leave a door open.
what: Approaching people and listening, with no conditions attached.
Handing out food, water and hygiene products.
Referral to specialist services where appropriate.
calle.who: The 2024 and 2025 reports document outreach in several areas of the Madrid region.
calle.note: These locations reflect outreach recorded in our annual reports. They are not permanent service points or fixed routes: to ask for help, phone or email is far more direct.

formacion.name: Training and personal development
formacion.short: Getting a skill back is part of getting a life back.
formacion.intro: Workshops are part of everyday life in the home. They give shape to the day, rebuild confidence and, in some cases, open a door to work.
formacion.who: People taking part in the programmes run by the association.
formacion.note: This is the list of workshops recorded in the 2024 and 2025 reports. What is actually running at any given time depends on the period and on available resources.

reinsercion.name: Social reintegration
reinsercion.intro: Reintegration is not just about finding a job. It is about independence, keeping a routine going, rebuilding relationships and feeling part of somewhere again.
what: Personal independence and managing daily life.
Preparing for life outside the home.
reinsercion.who: People who are making progress and beginning to prepare to leave the residential programme.

basicas.name: Basic needs
basicas.short: The essentials, when there is nothing.
basicas.intro: Before any longer process can begin, there are needs that will not wait. The 2025 report records the material support the association provides on an ongoing basis.
what: Transport for medical and administrative appointments.
basicas.who: People living in the home and those we meet through street outreach.
basicas.note: Much of this comes from private donations and from surplus food collected at markets.

hero.label: What we do
hero.title: Seven ways of walking alongside.
hero.lead: Our work is not a single programme. It is a sequence of supports that adapt to where each person is. This is what our annual activity reports describe.

hero.label: I need help
hero.title: You do not have to face this alone.
hero.lead: If you are living with an addiction, or supporting someone who is, you can talk to us. You do not need to have anything prepared or decided.

help.callBody: The most direct way to reach us is by phone. If you would rather write, you can email us or use the form on this page.
help.whatBody: We are a non-profit association with a residential home in Quijorna (Madrid) and an administrative office in the city. We support people affected by addiction and social vulnerability. According to the documentation published by the association, our services are free of charge.
offer: To listen, without judging you and without conditions.
To explain how our residential programme works.
Guidance for your family as well.
Basic needs such as food and hygiene products.
A referral to a more specialised service if that is what you need.
help.limitsBody: We are not a medical facility or an emergency service. We do not provide medical detoxification or psychiatric treatment. When a situation calls for specialist professional care, we refer: in 2025 we accompanied 22 people to Asociación Betel for exactly this reason.
help.emergencyBody: In a medical emergency or when there is an immediate risk to life, call 112. It is the emergency number across Spain and it answers 24 hours a day.
help.prepareBody: Three things help us point you in the right direction. You do not need to give medical details or say more than you want to.
prepare: Whether you are writing for yourself or for someone else.
A phone number or email where we can reach you.
help.privacyNote: Please do not send medical reports or health data through this form. When that needs discussing, we will do it directly with you.
help.processBody: We will get in touch to talk through your situation without rushing and to explain how the programme works. Access to a place in the home depends on availability at the time and is considered case by case.

hero.label: About us
hero.title: An association born out of experience.
hero.lead: Hogares Victoria began in 1986 in a neighbourhood of Lima and continues today in Madrid. In between lie four decades of people who chose to walk others through what they had been through themselves.

identity.label: Identity
identity.title: Who we are
identity.body1: Asociación Hogares Victoria de España is a non-profit civil body, Christian in inspiration, entered in the National Register of Associations of the Spanish Ministry of the Interior under number 626775.
identity.body2: We provide residential care and whole-person support for people with addiction problems and in situations of social vulnerability. Our work covers guidance, prevention, rehabilitation and reintegration, and is provided free of charge.

origin.label: Origin
origin.title: Barrios Altos, 1986.
origin.body1: On 30 April 1986, Hogares Victoria — then called Centro Victoria — began its work in Barrios Altos, in central Lima. Its purpose was to offer support and a route to restoration for people, especially young people, affected by alcohol and drugs.
origin.body2: Over the years the movement spread to countries across South America, North America and parts of Central America. The association's previous website stated that there were more than a hundred homes worldwide; that figure is still to be confirmed, which is why we do not present it here as current.

about.foundersBody: Luis and Vangie Salazar founded Hogares Victoria Internacional, the organisation the Spanish project belongs to.

spain.label: Spain
spain.title: Madrid, since 2023.
spain.body1: The 2025 financial report puts the association's activity in Madrid at around two and a half years during that financial year. The Spanish project brings together residential care, prevention, community outreach and reintegration.
spain.body2: The association currently runs two sites: the residential home in Quijorna, where the programme itself takes place, and an administrative office in Madrid for management, coordination and external enquiries.

about.mission: To walk alongside those struggling with addiction with whole-person support, love and hope in Christ. Through counselling, discipleship and spiritual restoration, we seek to help each person find a new purpose and become an agent of change for their family and their community.
about.vision: To be a home where every person finds the support, the hope and the love of Christ they need to restore their life and begin again.
about.expectation: To widen the network of homes in Spain and across Europe so as to reach more people in vulnerable situations, offering both practical and spiritual support and teaching values that help family and social reintegration.
about.expectationNote: This is an aspiration for the future, not a network that already exists across Europe.

values.name: Dignity
values.body: Nobody is reduced to their addiction. Everyone who comes through the door arrives with a whole life behind them.

values.name: Shared experience
values.body: The people doing the supporting know this road from the inside. That changes how they listen.

values.name: Living together
values.body: The home is not a service. It is a house, with routines, shared meals and chores that get divided up.

values.name: Shared responsibility
values.body: We walk alongside people; we do not do it for them. Each person carries their own process.

values.name: Free of charge
values.body: What someone can afford does not decide whether they get help.

values.name: Hope
values.body: Christian faith sustains this work. It is not a requirement for being welcomed.

about.faithTitle: Where this way of seeing comes from
about.faithBody: Hogares Victoria is a Christian-inspired organisation. That faith is why we believe no life is beyond reach, and why the door stays open after a relapse. Two biblical passages the organisation uses carry particular weight in our identity: Psalm 72:12-15 and 1 Samuel 2:8, both about lifting up those who cannot lift themselves.
about.faithNote: We do not reproduce the text of these passages here: the wording depends on the translation and on its terms of use.
about.teamBody: The association is led by Pastor Alfredo Pedraza Soriano. Institutional documents from 2025 also record Silvie Yvonne Espinel Bello as secretary.
about.teamNote: Roles and team photographs are still to be confirmed, and require the express authorisation of the people involved.
about.ctaTitle: Here is what all of this looks like day to day.
about.ctaBody: The concrete side of our work — the home, the sessions, the street, the workshops — is set out on the what we do page.

origen.title: Centro Victoria opens in Lima
origen.body: On 30 April 1986, in Barrios Altos, central Lima, the work that would later be known as Hogares Victoria begins.

expansion.title: The movement spreads
expansion.body: Over almost four decades, the organisation extends to countries across South America, North America and parts of Central America.

espana.title: Hogares Victoria arrives in Madrid
espana.body: Work begins in Spain, with an administrative office on Avenida de Badajoz and the first outreach in areas of the city where drug use is active.

quijorna.title: The residential home opens in Quijorna
quijorna.body: The 2024 financial report records three months of rent for the home at Calle Real 31, placing its opening in the final stretch of the year.

consolidacion.title: A year of consolidation
consolidacion.body: In 2025 the residential service runs continuously all year: 38 people supported in the homes and more than 420 individual and group sessions.

congreso.title: Congress of the Republic of Peru
congreso.body: Congress recognised 23 pastors for more than thirty years of missionary and social work. The available documentation records the ceremony but not its exact date.

chorrillos.title: Chorrillos Town Council
chorrillos.body: The association's previous website recorded a recognition from Chorrillos Town Council awarded to Pastor Alfredo Pedraza. No date is recorded.

recognitions.note: We present these recognitions exactly as they appear in the organisation's documentation, without claiming more for them than they are.

hero.label: Impact and transparency
hero.title: Clear accounts, work in plain sight.
hero.lead: We publish our activity reports and our financial reports in full. They are summarised here, and the original documents can be downloaded complete.

impact.note2025: Figures taken from the 2025 Annual Activity Report. They cover that year alone and are not cumulative.
impact.note2024: Figures taken from the 2024 Activity Report.
impact.discrepancyTitle: A discrepancy we are not hiding
impact.discrepancyBody: The 2024 report states that «more than 280 individual and group sessions» took place, but its own breakdown gives 260 group and 60 individual sessions, which add up to 320. We will not publish a reconciled figure until the association confirms which is correct.
impact.noAggregationTitle: Why we do not add these figures up
impact.noAggregationBody: The people supported in the homes, those in the outpatient programme and those referred elsewhere may partly be the same people. Adding them together would produce a total number of beneficiaries that is simply not real.
impact.comparisonBody: Two consecutive years, each with its own figures. The first full year of the Quijorna home accounts for much of the difference.
impact.financeTitle: Where every euro comes from and where it goes
impact.financeBody: In {year} the association received {income} and spent {expenses}, leaving a surplus of {surplus}. It received no public funding.
impact.fundingBody: The main source of funding is private generosity: donations, membership fees and the sale of keyrings and crafts made in the association's own workshops. Transfers from the parent organisation in Peru add to this. Neither of the two published financial years records any public funding.
impact.docsBody: These are the complete documents, exactly as signed by the directors of the association. They are written in Spanish.
impact.ctaBody: Every euro that comes in shows up in next year's report.

hero.label: Volunteer
hero.title: Your time can change a life too.
hero.lead: Much of what happens at Hogares Victoria is held up by volunteers. The 2025 report says so in as many words: volunteering is a key element in the sustainability of the project.

volunteer.whatBody: Volunteering here is very concrete: joining a street outreach shift, helping run a workshop, assisting with paperwork, driving the van, preparing a meal, simply being around. You do not need to be a specialist. You do need to be reliable and respectful.
volunteer.whyBody: For someone nobody has asked after in months, one steady presence can change the mood of a whole week. And for the team, every extra pair of hands widens what can be done without widening the budget.

legal.reviewNoticeBody: This document sets out a professional structure drafted from the information available, but it has not yet been reviewed or approved by a legal adviser. It should not be treated as a final legal text.

sections.heading: Identifying details
sections.body: In compliance with the duty of information set out in Spanish Law 34/2002 on Information Society Services and Electronic Commerce, the following details are published: owner, Asociación Hogares Victoria de España; tax ID G56681133; entered in the National Register of Associations of the Ministry of the Interior, Section 1, number 626775; registered address at Calle Real 31, Quijorna (Madrid); telephone +34 647 672 300; email info@hogaresvictoria.es.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: This website exists to provide information about the activity of the association and to allow visitors to get in touch, request information and make donations through external providers.

sections.heading: Terms of use
sections.body: Accessing this site implies acceptance of these terms. Users undertake to make proper use of its contents and not to use them for unlawful purposes or in ways harmful to others.

sections.heading: Intellectual property
sections.body: The texts, logo and photographs on this site belong to Asociación Hogares Victoria de España or are used with its permission. They may not be reproduced without prior consent.

sections.heading: External links
sections.body: This site contains links to third-party services such as PayPal and YouTube. The association is not responsible for the content or the privacy policies of those services.

sections.heading: Accuracy of information
sections.body: The information published about programmes, activities and results comes from the official annual reports of the association. The association does not guarantee the permanent availability of every service described, which depends on the resources available at any given time.

sections.heading: Data controller
sections.body: Asociación Hogares Victoria de España, tax ID G56681133, registered address Calle Real 31, Quijorna (Madrid). Contact email: info@hogaresvictoria.es.

sections.heading: What data we collect
sections.body: Only what you voluntarily provide through the contact and volunteering forms: name, email address, phone number if you give one, reason for contact and the content of your message. This website does not use advertising profiles and does not build behavioural profiles.

sections.heading: Health data
sections.body: We do not request medical information or health data through this website, and we ask you not to include any in the forms. If something of that kind needs discussing, we will do it through a direct channel with you.

sections.heading: What we use it for
sections.body: Solely to respond to your enquiry and, where relevant, to keep in touch about that enquiry. We do not pass your data to third parties and we do not use it to send you marketing.

sections.heading: Legal basis
sections.body: The consent you give when submitting the form, and the legitimate interest of the association in responding to the enquiries it receives.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
sections.body: For as long as is needed to deal with your enquiry and, afterwards, for any legally required retention periods. Once that period has passed, the data is deleted.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You can request access to, rectification of, erasure of, restriction of or portability of your data, and object to its processing, by writing to info@hogaresvictoria.es. You may also lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD).

sections.heading: External providers
sections.body: Donations are processed through PayPal, which acts as an independent data controller. Videos are hosted on YouTube and only load when you choose to play them. Hosting this website and delivering the forms may involve processing by technical providers under the corresponding data processing agreements.

sections.heading: Our own cookies
sections.body: This website uses a single technical cookie to remember the language you have chosen. It is necessary for the site to work and does not require consent.

sections.heading: External services
sections.body: YouTube videos do not load automatically: a connection to that service is only made when you press play. At that point YouTube may set its own cookies, subject to its privacy policy.

sections.heading: Analytics
sections.body: This website does not include analytics or advertising tracking tools. If any were added in future, a consent mechanism compliant with the applicable regulations would be implemented first.

sections.heading: How to manage them
sections.body: You can delete or block cookies from your browser settings. Doing so does not prevent you from using this site, although your language choice will no longer be remembered between visits.
